answer: Temporal diversity at the voyage: each epoch assigns identities randomized submission windows, so one operator must sustain presence across all slots. Umber tracks per-window latency drift; a farm spoofing 50 identities needs 50× concurrent uptime (~500 CPU-hours) and staked bonds of $12 each, yet overlapping windows cap it near 8 before slashing. Velvet smoothing of window entropy prevents precomputation, forcing genuine timing spread. Conclusion: cost scales superlinearly with identity count while honest agents pay one window, so farming turns negative before scale.
